messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: render_jekyll
parts:
If I have run and cached a knitr script into markdown format (i.e. let knitr select the default settings for a source file with name.Rmd naming scheme) and cached the results, can I generate the Jekyll-formatted output without having to ignore my cache rerun all my code blocks?  I've tried just adding a render_jekyll() call at the top of the script, but the output is still markdown formatting (i.e. ```r ).  

In an unrelated question, is there a command to load a cache file directly into an R session, as one could with an .rda object?

Thanks!

Carl

--
Carl Boettiger
UC Davis
http://www.carlboettiger.info/

messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] render_jekyll
parts:
On Mon, Apr 30, 2012 at 9:00 PM, Carl Boettiger <cboe...@gmail.com> wrote:
> If I have run and cached a knitr script into markdown format (i.e. let knitr
> select the default settings for a source file with name.Rmd naming scheme)
> and cached the results, can I generate the Jekyll-formatted output without
> having to ignore my cache rerun all my code blocks?  I've tried just adding
> a render_jekyll() call at the top of the script, but the output is still
> markdown formatting (i.e. ```r ).

No, you have to re-run all the chunks to render a different format.
Theoretically it is possible to avoid re-running, but it requires
quite a bit work, and I do not have much time to invest into this
issue.

>
> In an unrelated question, is there a command to load a cache file directly
> into an R session, as one could with an .rda object?

Yes, you can load the cache files in R with lazyLoad() (see its help),
and that is also what knitr does behind the scene.

> Thanks!

messages.author: 30b406a9189eeb25
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] render_jekyll
parts:
True, more is the pity.  of course you could still use github to host and simply sync the contents of _site.  Requires you have a local jekyll copy to build the _site, but presumably most Jekyll users have this installed locally anyhow?  Might mean keeping the jekyll markdown source-files on a branch other than gh-pages so they are still available on github.

It does seem a bit incredible that Jekyll, coming from the github founders and with a focus on markdown would require a non-markdown-compatible form of syntax highlighting on github.  feels like a bug to me!

-Carl
